design.affected_system: land-use planning, public investment, regeneration, and community-benefit system
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits
pair minimum-benefit, need, deliverability, and displacement-risk allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Parcels, zoning, ownership, development, business, housing, public assets, and population use dated versions.
Scenario capacity and market response are not treated as approved projects or inevitable change.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain the current distribution rule for regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits.

constraints.description: The land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: planning director and neighborhood regeneration commissioner
design.decision_question: How should capital, land value, grants, affordable space, jobs, and public benefits be distributed?
design.family_title: Land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change

independence_key.binding_constraint: The land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.decision_object: regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: minimum-benefit, need, deliverability, and displacement-risk allocation
independence_key.primary_outcome: verified community priorities without funded enforceable benefit

design.intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: verified community priorities without funded enforceable benefit
distributional gap in verified community priorities without funded enforceable benefit
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present modeled allocations as negotiated, legally secured, funded, or delivered benefits.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for regeneration funding and enforceable community benefits passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

design.title: Allocate regeneration funds and community benefits
transportability_risks: Planning law, property rights, finance, markets, institutions, and community priorities differ.
Parcel and transaction data may miss informal tenure, businesses, and cultural assets.

family.affected_system: land-use planning, public investment, regeneration, and community-benefit system
claim_boundary: Requests, listings, parcels, and administrative records do not alone verify conditions or need.
Screened sites and portfolios are not permits, acquisitions, adopted plans, or completed housing.
Displacement, affordability, habitability, and program effects require direct outcomes and identification.
family.decision_owner: planning director and neighborhood regeneration commissioner
family.description: Eight decisions for land diagnosis, development forecasting, public investment portfolios, facility siting, benefit allocation, phasing, market stress, and regeneration evaluation.
family.title: Land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
